"County (United States)") in the [U.S. state](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/U.S._state "U.S. state") of [North Dakota](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/North_Dakota "North Dakota"). As of the [2020 census](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_United_States_census "2020 United States census"), the population was 184,525,[\[1\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cass_County,_North_Dakota#cite_note-2020_Census_\(City\)-1) making it the [most populous county in North Dakota](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_counties_in_North_Dakota "List of counties in North Dakota"), and was estimated to be 200,945 in 2024, almost twice the population of [Burleigh County](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Burleigh_County,_North_Dakota "Burleigh County, North Dakota"), the second most populated county in the state.[\[2\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cass_County,_North_Dakota#cite_note-QF-2) It contains over 25.23% of the state's population.[\[3\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cass_County,_North_Dakota#cite_note-3) The [county seat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/County_seat "County seat") is [Fargo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fargo,_North_Dakota "Fargo, North Dakota"),[\[4\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cass_County,_North_Dakota#cite_note-4) the state's [most populous city](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_cities_in_North_Dakota "List of cities in North Dakota"). The county is named for [George Washington Cass](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_Washington_Cass "George Washington Cass"), president of the [Northern Pacific Railway](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Northern_Pacific_Railway "Northern Pacific Railway") from 1872 to 1875. It is the only Cass County in the United States that is not named after [Lewis Cass](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lewis_Cass "Lewis Cass"). Cass County is part of the [Fargo, ND-Moorhead, MN Metropolitan Statistical Area](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fargo%E2%80%93Moorhead "Fargo–Moorhead"). Cass County was defined by action of the [Dakota Territory](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dakota_Territory "Dakota Territory") legislature on January 4, 1873, and its organization was affected on October 27 of that year. It was named for railroad executive [George Washington Cass](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_Washington_Cass "George Washington Cass") (1810–1888).[\[5\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cass_County,_North_Dakota#cite_note-5) Its boundaries were altered in 1875, and in 1961.[\[6\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cass_County,_North_Dakota#cite_note-6)[\[7\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cass_County,_North_Dakota#cite_note-7) Cass County lies on the east side of North Dakota. Its east boundary line abuts the west boundary line of the state of [Minnesota](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Minnesota "Minnesota") across the river. The [Red River](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Red_River_of_the_North "Red River of the North") flows northward along the county's east boundary, on its way to Lake Winnipeg and Hudson Bay. The county's terrain consists of low rolling hills, devoted to agriculture except around developed areas.[\[8\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cass_County,_North_Dakota#cite_note-CCND-8) Its terrain slopes to the north and east, with its highest point on the southwestern corner at 1,194 ft (364 m) ASL.[\[9\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cass_County,_North_Dakota#cite_note-9) According to the [United States Census Bureau](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Census_Bureau "United States Census Bureau"), the county has a total area of 1,767.811 square miles (4,578.61 km2), of which 1,764.935 square miles (4,571.16 km2) is land and 2.876 square miles (7.45 km2) (0.16%) is water.[\[10\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cass_County,_North_Dakota#cite_note-10) It is the 10th largest county in North Dakota by total area.[\[11\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cass_County,_North_Dakota#cite_note-11) * [Amtrak](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amtrak "Amtrak") _[Empire Builder](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Empire_Builder "Empire Builder")_ (_[Fargo station](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fargo_station "Fargo station")_) * [Jefferson Lines](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jefferson_Lines "Jefferson Lines") * [MATBUS](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MATBUS_/(Fargo-Moorhead/) "MATBUS (Fargo-Moorhead)") * [Traill County](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Traill_County,_North_Dakota "Traill County, North Dakota") - As of the fourth quarter of 2024, the median home value in Cass County was $301,108.[\[17\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cass_County,_North_Dakota#cite_note-17) As of the 2023 [American Community Survey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_Community_Survey "American Community Survey"), there are 81,668 estimated households in Cass County with an average of 2.24 persons per household. The county has a median household income of $75,023. As recently as the 2004 presidential election, [George W. Bush](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_W._Bush "George W. Bush") carried Cass County with nearly 60 percent of the vote. However, in recent elections, the county has become more politically diverse and competitive, particularly in Fargo. In 2008, Democratic candidate [Barack Obama](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barack_Obama "Barack Obama") won the majority of votes in Cass County, with a voting percentage very close to the percentage Obama received in the entire nation, while [John McCain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_McCain "John McCain") won the majority of votes in North Dakota. [Mitt Romney](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mitt_Romney "Mitt Romney")'s winning margin in 2012 over Obama in Cass County was 49.9% to 47%, while [Donald Trump](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Donald_Trump "Donald Trump") received 49.3% of votes in 2016 (52.69% in 2024), compared to 38.8% for [Hillary Clinton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hillary_Clinton "Hillary Clinton") and 11.9% for third-party candidates. Share

"X (Twitter)")[LinkedIn](https://www.linkedin.com/sharing/share-offsite/?url=https://www.census.gov/data/what-is-data-census-gov/guidance-for-data-users/frequently-asked-questions/how-can-i-find-data-for-zip-codes-on-data-census-gov.html&title=How+can+I+find+data+for+ZIP+Codes+on+data.census.gov%3F&text=If+you+have+tried+accessing+data.census.gov+and+you+receive+an+error+message+that+provides+a+Support+ID%2C+please+check...&source=U.S.+Census+Bureau "LinkedIn")

 

The Census Bureau produces economic data for ZIP Codes as defined by the United States Postal Service.

For demographic and housing data from the decennial census or American Community Survey (ACS), the Census Bureau uses generalized representations of ZIP Codes through a geography called ZIP Code Tabulation Areas (ZCTAs). If you would like to learn more about this type of geography and how they differ from the mail delivery routes that ZIP codes are based on, check out this [geography webpage](https://www.census.gov/programs-surveys/geography/guidance/geo-areas/zctas.html) and [short video](https://www.census.gov/data/academy/data-gems/2018/zcta.html).

**How to Select ZIP Code Tabulation Areas (ZCTAs) to Get Demographic Data**

Click the “ZIP Code Tabulation Area” option using the geography [filters on data.census.gov](https://data.census.gov/advanced). This provides data through Summary Level 860 from the decennial census and American Community Survey.

Geography: ZIP Code Tabulation Area

[![Image 6: How can I find data for ZIP Codes on data.census.gov? Please note:

*   American Community Survey tables were not produced for ZCTAs prior to the 2011 ACS 5-year release.

**How to Select ZIP Codes to Get Economic Data**

Use the option titled “5-digit ZIP Code” in the geography [filters on data.census.gov](https://data.census.gov/advanced). This provides data through Summary Level 861 from the Business Patterns program.

Geography: All Geographies → 5-digit ZIP Code

Important Cass, ND Information ------------------------------ * * * Cass County, ND Covers 39 ZIP Codes. This includes 24 Standard ZIP Codes, 5 PO Box ZIP Codes, and 5 Unique (reserved for Business and Volume Mail Receivers). There are also 5 Multi County ZIP Codes. These records are assigned a different primary county, but they partially cover area in Cass County. The population for Cass County is 184,525, according to the U.S. Census. Population Density is 104.55 persons per square mile. With 85,397 Housing Units, the Average Household Size is 2.27 persons. There are 78,672 Family Households with an Average Family Size of 3.03 persons. 5.15% of the population is without Health Insurance. The 73.82% Employment Rate is 14.02% above the national average of 59.8%.119,321 people aged 25+ have some educational achievement, with 43.28% (or 51,648 people) having attained a Bachelor's Degree or higher.[More Demographics](https://www.zip-codes.com/county/nd-cass.asp#demographics) are available below. [701](https://www.zip-codes.com/area-code/area-code-701.asp "Area Code 701") is the only area code for this area. Cass is also located in the Central (GMT -06:00) timezone and the current local time is shown above. Cass is part of the Fargo, ND-MN Core Based Statistical Area (CBSA). Its CBSA Code is 22020.It is classified as a metro area, which means the combined population is 50,000 or more (at its core). CBSAs are defined by the OMB as geographic areas that have at least one core with a population of 10,000 or more (for a micro area) and adjacent territory with a high degree of social and economic integration. CBSA codes are commonly used to accurately file Medicare claims and to verify applicable incentives using a patient's ZIP Code. ZIP Codes in Cass, ND have 89,977 Residential mailboxes and 5,910 Business mailboxes.There are 5,997 businesses with a total of 112,689 employees. That is an average of 18.8 employees per business.
